newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB shares drop after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB shares drop after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in satellite broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting Plc dropped in early trading on Wednesday after the company posted first-half profits no better than analysts had expected.

BSkyB said pre-tax profit rose to 133.7 million stg in the six months ended December 31 from 106.3 million stg a year before. Analyst forecasts had mostly been in a range between 131 million stg and 138 million.
"They are good results but they are basically in line with expectations," said Louise Barton, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
The stock was down 8p at 585 by 0818 GMT, after on Monday climbing to their highest level in over three months.
Barton said the company's plan to take a 49 percent stake in German digital TV operation DF1, where BSkyB said it was considering investments in additional pay-TV channels, was a potential concern.
But she said the company had taken out its most significant likely UK threat by linking with Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc's digital TV venture.
"They have ended up a part of it which is obviously very positive," Barton said. "We are happy to remain holders of the stock."
Carlo Campomagnani, analyst at Lehman Brothers, also said the results were little different from what he had expected.
"They are bang in line with our numbers," he said.
BSkyB chief executive Sam Chisholm said the results showed the company had increased profits while continuing to make substantial investments to strengthen its programme schedules.
"BSkyB is now extremely well-positioned to capitalise on the introduction of digital television and the significant benefits that will flow from this new technology," he said.
BSkyB said dish sales and new cable connections tend to be stronger in the first half and were therefore expected to grow at a slower rate in the second half of the year.
However the significant growth in the subscriber base in the first six months gave potential for increased revenues in the second half, it said.
